<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-cottage-cheese" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-cottage-cheese-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of cottage cheese, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

No maximum level for metals in cottage cheese was verified from primary text for this page; buyers should confirm the limit that applies in the destination market.

## Cottage cheese FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-cottage-cheese" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-cottage-cheese" data-question="What heavy metals are found in cottage cheese?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in cottage cheese?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ba, Hg, Sr and Ti in cottage cheese, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-cottage-cheese-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-cottage-cheese-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of cottage cheese measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of cottage cheese measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 8 groups of cottage cheese ranged from 8.9 µg/kg (farm K, Almaty region (sample K/1-5-1-1)) to 16.2 µg/kg (farm A, Almaty region (sample A/1-5-1-5)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/sarsembayeva2020-almaty-milk-fermented-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sarsembayeva NB, Abdigaliyeva TB, Utepova ZA, Biltebay AN, Zhumagulova SZ · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sarsembayeva2020-almaty-milk-fermented-metals">Heavy metal levels in milk and fermented milk products produced in the Almaty region, Kazakhstan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Veterinary World 13(4):609-613</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sarsembayeva2020-almaty-milk-fermented-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, total mercury across 8 groups of cottage cheese ranged from 40 µg/kg (producer C (code 9C)) to 230 µg/kg (producer A (code 7A)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/pankiewicz2012-thg-dairy-products-poland|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Pankiewicz U · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/pankiewicz2012-thg-dairy-products-poland">Monitoring of total mercury level in selected dairy products from the south-east regions of Poland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Ecological Chemistry and Engineering A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/pankiewicz2012-thg-dairy-products-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
